title: people-ops-hiring-onboarding-performance-and-manager-guide-2026-v110
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Summary:
This guide documents Redwood Inference's standard hiring process, the new-employee onboarding program, the performance and feedback cycle, and key expectations for managers. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering/product leaders.

Scope:
Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hires in North America and Europe. Private/offsite or regulated-customer hiring steps may add compliance checkpoints (see Related Pages).

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-offer while maintaining candidate quality and EEO compliance.
- Deliver a consistent 30-60-90 onboarding experience that enables new hires to contribute safely and productively.
- Create a predictable, fair performance and feedback cadence focused on development and calibration.

1) Hiring process: end-to-end standard operating procedure

Quick facts and targets:
- Target time-to-fill (req open -> accepted offer): 45 calendar days (company benchmark).
- Target interview-to-offer time: 7 business days.
- Offer acceptance target: >= 70%.
- Recruiter response SLA to hiring manager and candidate: 48 hours.

Stages and responsibilities (numbered):
1. Requisition creation (Hiring manager + People Ops):
   - Completion checklist: role brief, salary band, interview panel, target diversity channels.
   - People Ops owner: Aisha Patel.
2. Sourcing & outreach (Recruiting team):
   - Use prioritized channels: company career site, internal referrals, targeted sourcing, diversity pipelines.
   - Passive candidate outreach cadence: 3-touch outreach over two weeks.
3. Resume screen & phone screen (Recruiter):
   - Recruiter ensures baseline fit and salary expectation alignment before scheduling.
   - Standard phone screen scorecard (see Appendix).
4. Interview loop (Hiring manager sets panel):
   - Typical loop (technical IC): Recruiter screen -> 60-min technical deep-dive -> 45-min system design -> 30-min behavioral/culture -> Hiring manager debrief.
   - For senior hires include hiring manager + peer + cross-functional stakeholder.
5. Calibration & debrief (Panel):
   - Hold debrief within 48 hours. Use scorecard normalization matrix.
6. Offer approval (Hiring manager + People Ops + Finance):
   - Final comp sign-off required by People Ops and Finance for roles above band midpoint.
7. Offer extension + negotiation (Recruiter):
   - Send written offer with 5-business-day expiration unless otherwise approved.
8. Background checks & references (People Ops):
   - Initiate after verbal acceptance; employment contingent on satisfactory background checks.
9. Candidate experience & feedback:
   - Send timely updates after each stage; recruiters to provide candidate feedback within 3 business days after decision.

Interview scorecard (standard fields) - use these in every loop:
- Role-specific competencies (technical/problem solving) scored 1-5
- System design / architecture (1-5)
- Collaboration & communication (1-5)
- Ownership & execution (1-5)
- Culture add & values alignment (pass/needs-discussion)
- Overall recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / No Hire / Needs Follow-up

Sample interviewer rubric (text table):
| Competency              | 1 - Needs work                | 3 - Meets expectations         | 5 - Exceeds expectations       |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Problem solving         | Struggled to reason clearly   | Solved with standard approach | Creative, efficient solution  |
| System design           | Incomplete / missing tradeoffs| Solid design with tradeoffs   | Elegant, scalable solution    |

EEO & anti-bias rules:
- Ask only job-relevant questions. Avoid personal demographic questions.
- Use structured scorecards to reduce bias.
- Any candidate flagged by an interviewer for potential accommodation must be escalated to People Ops.

2) Offer & compensation guidance

Salary bands and equity:
- Use published band ranges for role leveling; bands owned by People Ops and Finance.
- For senior roles a comp packet requires VP approval.

Offer templates (summary):
- Base salary, equity grant summary, target bonus (if applicable), start date, reporting manager, remote/location expectations, onboarding start details, termination policy, employment-at-will notice (where applicable).

Negotiation guardrails:
- Hiring managers can approve up to band midpoint. Anything above requires People Ops sign-off.
- Counteroffer timeframe: 72 hours.

3) Onboarding program (first 90 days)

Philosophy:
Onboarding is not a single day; it is a structured ramp designed to build product, platform, and cultural context while giving early contributions.

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- People Ops checklist: hardware ordered, Slack account provisioned, initial calendar with 1:1, team orientation, security training, and access requests submitted.
- Manager checklist: welcome email, first-week objectives, buddy assignment.

Day 1-7 (orientation + baseline):
- Day 1: HR/People Ops orientation (policies, benefits, payroll), facilities/IT setup, security training.
- End of week 1: technical environment validated, initial 30-day goals set, 1:1 with manager and buddy pairing confirmed.

30-60-90 plan (template):
- 30 days (Observe & learn): Understand codebase, deploy a non-prod change, complete compliance training.
- 60 days (Contribute): Deliver first small project, own a recurring operational task (e.g., runbook updates).
- 90 days (Impact): Lead a cross-team initiative, undergo performance calibration with manager.

Onboarding deliverables and checkpoints (table format described):
- Week 2: Security & access audit (owner: IT).
- Week 4: Manager checkpoint (owner: Hiring manager).
- Day 60: Skills review & training plan (owner: People Ops + Manager).
- Day 90: Formal onboarding close & success rubric evaluation (owner: Manager).

New-hire buddy program:
- All new hires are assigned a buddy for 90 days. Buddy responsibilities include codebase orientation, social introductions, and weekly check-ins for the first month.

4) Performance and feedback cycles

Cadence and components:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged ad-hoc and documented in the performance system.
- Formal 1:1s: weekly for first 90 days, then at least bi-weekly for ongoing hires.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager + employee focused on goals, blockers, and career development.
- Annual performance review: calibration across teams with leveling and compensation changes.

Performance rating scale (text):
- Exceeds expectations (A)
- Meets expectations (B)
- Needs improvement (C)

Probationary and improvement plans:
- For new hires, the first 90 days is an active ramp. If performance concerns arise, manager should open a documented Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with People Ops within 10 business days of the identified concern.

Calibration & fairness:
- Managers submit calibrated ratings and narrative in the performance portal. Calibration committees review for bias and consistency.
- People Ops runs statistical checks for grade inflation and demographic parity.

Feedback best practices (for managers):
- Use timely, specific examples.
- Balance positive reinforcement with development areas.
- Document actions and follow-ups in the performance system.

5) Manager responsibilities & manager onboarding

Manager expectations in hiring and onboarding:
- Build inclusive interview panels and complete interviewer training annually.
- Provide clear role briefs and agreed success metrics before opening a req.
- Complete offer discussions promptly and support negotiation within guardrails.

Manager checklist for new hires (first 30 days):
- Day 0: Send welcome message and first-week plan.
- Day 1: Conduct role orientation and set expectations.
- Week 1: Introduce new hire to cross-functional partners.
- Week 2: Establish 30-60-90 goals and document in performance system.

Manager development resources:
- Interviewer training deck (link in Related Pages).
- Inclusive hiring playbook (link in Related Pages).
- Coaching templates and sample feedback scripts (Appendix).

6) People policies and templates (operational reference)

Included templates and where to find them:
- Job brief template (use for requisition creation).
- Interview scorecard (required).
- Offer letter templates (US/EMEA).
- 30-60-90 plan template.
- PIP template and legal checklist.

Security & compliance checkpoints for private/on-prem roles:
- Additional background checks, customer-specific NDAs, and approval from Security & Legal required before offer acceptance.

7) Escalations and dispute resolution

Common escalations:
- Compensation disputes: escalate to People Ops and Finance.
- Offer rescind requests: People Ops lead + Legal involvement.
- Candidate allegations of bias: escalate to People Ops and DEI for investigation.

Escalation process (simple steps):
1. Notify People Ops within 24 hours.
2. People Ops triage and assign owner.
3. Resolve or escalate to Legal/DEI within 5 business days.

Appendix: sample interview scorecard (example JSON-like text for copy/paste)
{
  "candidate_name": "Candidate Example",
  "role": "Senior Software Engineer",
  "interviewer": "Name",
  "scores": {"problem_solving": 4, "system_design": 3, "communication": 4},
  "overall_recommendation": "Hire"
}

Appendix: sample 30-60-90 template (plain text)
- 30 days: Complete onboarding checklist, fix first bug in dev cluster, meet top 10 stakeholders.
- 60 days: Deliver first minor feature, run one incident postmortem.
- 90 days: Lead feature planning, present onboarding review to team.

Ownership & maintenance
- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: annual review each January; interim updates for process changes.

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: What if a hiring manager needs to expedite a hire?
A: Mark the req as expedited in Greenhouse, notify People Ops; expedited hires require a streamlined 48-hour panel window and People Ops approval for comp.

Q: Who approves exceptions to offers?
A: Exceptions above band midpoint require People Ops + Finance sign-off; exceptions to policy (e.g., retaining contractors beyond 12 months) require Legal approval.
